info.name: RAN Online GS Payments & Recharge API — 2026-10-16
info.description: Source-derived examples. Fill session_cookie (value of the player session cookie after login) and admin_jwt (from POST /admin/v1/auth/authenticate). No credentials included. Webhook requests are unsigned in the current implementation and would change real transactions.

request.description:
Returns every RechargeInfo row with RechargeStatus = 1 as a bare JSON array. No session is read; the cookie session middleware still wraps the scope but never rejects. No pagination, no ordering clause (SQL Server row order), no caching (the generic cache is a TODO). The `type` of each package decides which payment method POST /transaction/{id} will use.

Examples are fixtures. Mutating requests create real records if sent to a live server.

Returns the RechargeInfo row regardless of its status (inactive packages are readable here). A nil UUID (all zeroes) returns 400. A missing row is reported as 500, not 404, because the DB layer returns an error that the handler maps to 500.

Examples are fixtures. Mutating requests create real records if sent to a live server.

Requires a signed-in user session whose profile has is_verified = true. Loads the RechargeInfo by path ID, then dispatches on RechargeInfo.type:

- 1 GCash: body REQUIRED, `{"type":"gcash",...}`. Inserts a pending WebTransaction (type 1) with reference code and optional proof image; an administrator approves it later.
- 2 PayPal: body MUST BE ABSENT. Inserts a pending WebTransaction (type 2), creates a PayPal order (USD, intent CAPTURE, invoice_id = transaction UUID) and returns the PayPal approval URL. The PayPal webhook settles it.
- 3 Wise: body REQUIRED, `{"type":"wise",...}`. Inserts a pending WebTransaction (type 3) with reference code; an administrator approves it later.
- 4 PayMongo: body MUST BE ABSENT. Inserts a pending WebTransaction (type 4), creates a PayMongo checkout session (PHP centavos, card + gcash, metadata.transaction_id = transaction UUID) and returns its checkout URL as approval_url. The PayMongo webhook settles it.

The body extractor is Option<Json<TransactionPayload>>: an unparseable, wrong-content-type or oversized (>2 MiB actix default) body is silently treated as absent. Sending a body to a PayPal/PayMongo package, or the wrong tag for the package type, returns 400 'Invalid transaction data'. A Discord notification is spawned after GCash/Wise inserts. Points are credited only when the transaction status later becomes 1 (database trigger trg_AddWebPoints).

Examples are fixtures. Mutating requests create real records if sent to a live server.

request.description:
Requires a user session. Loads every WebTransaction of session.user_num ordered by TransactionTime DESC, filters in memory by `status` and `category` (= transaction type), then paginates in memory. `search`, `start_date`, `end_date` are accepted but ignored. Results are cached per (user_num, page, limit) for 30 seconds; the cache stores the unfiltered list, so filter changes apply immediately but newly created transactions can take up to 30 s to appear.

Examples are fixtures. Mutating requests create real records if sent to a live server.

Server-to-server, called by PayPal. NO signature verification is performed (the HMAC verifier is commented out), so anyone who can reach the URL can post events. Body is parsed as free-form JSON; only the fields in PayPalWebhookEvent are read. The handler checks, in order: `resource` present, `resource.id` string present, `event_type` present, then dispatches:

- CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED: captures the order through the PayPal API using resource.id. Does NOT change the transaction status; the later PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED does. Invalidates the buyer's profile cache when the invoice ID resolves.
- PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED: sets the transaction (invoice ID) to status 1 → trigger credits points; invalidates the profile cache.
- CHECKOUT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED: same branch, but its status mapping is 0, so it updates Pending→Pending (no effect).
- PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DENIED / PAYMENT.CAPTURE.DECLINED: sets status 2; update failures are only logged.
- anything else: acknowledged, not processed.

The transaction UUID (invoice ID) is read from resource.invoice_id, else resource.purchase_units[0].invoice_id, else resource.custom. Status updates only apply to Pending (0) rows; a repeat delivery after settlement fails the update and returns 500 for the COMPLETED branch.

Examples are fixtures. Mutating requests create real records if sent to a live server.

Server-to-server, called by PayMongo. NO signature verification (PayMongo-Signature check is commented out). The raw body is read as UTF-8 and parsed as PayMongoWebhookPayload. Event type = data.attributes.type:

- payment.paid: sets the transaction to status 1 → trigger credits points.
- payment.failed: sets the transaction to status 2.
- anything else: ignored.

The transaction UUID is data.attributes.data.attributes.metadata.transaction_id (copied by PayMongo from the checkout session metadata set at purchase). The handler ALWAYS answers 200 text/plain 'Webhook received and processed' once the payload parses — including unknown events, a missing transaction_id, and failed status updates — so PayMongo never retries those. The buyer's profile cache is NOT invalidated here (unlike PayPal).

query.description: SQL page index; OFFSET = page × limit (see quirk).
UserName substring or exact reference code.

request.description:
Primary admin transaction list. Query is parsed with serde_qs (max depth 5, non-strict, so percent-encoded brackets are accepted). Multi-value filters use bracket notation: `?status[]=0&status[]=1&method[]=1&method[]=4` (indexed `status[0]=0` also works). Empty arrays mean no filter. Calls sp_GetWebTransactions: `search` matches UserName LIKE '%search%' OR RefferenceCode = search; rows sort Pending first, then TransactionTime DESC.

PAGINATION QUIRK: the procedure computes OFFSET = page × limit, so it is effectively 0-based. page=1 (the default) skips the first `limit` rows; send page=0 for the first page. page/limit are cast from usize to i16 (truncating); limit is not clamped. Response has no total_pages.

Examples are fixtures. Mutating requests create real records if sent to a live server.

request.description:
Loads ALL WebTransaction rows (or all rows with the given status) ordered by TransactionTime DESC, then filters `category` and `search` and paginates in memory. `search` matches when user_name CONTAINS it (case-sensitive), or equals the transaction_id string, or equals reference_code. start_date/end_date are accepted but ignored. Every row's proof image is base64-encoded into the response. Prefer GET /admin/v1/recharge.

Examples are fixtures. Mutating requests create real records if sent to a live server.

The new status is a QUERY parameter, not a body (any body is ignored). Only rows still Pending (0) are updated; anything else returns 500. Setting 1 fires trigger trg_AddWebPoints, which adds transaction_amount (points) to the buyer's WebUser.WebPoints. Any i16 is accepted (no range check); use 1 (approve) or 2 (decline). On success: the buyer's profile cache is invalidated and a Discord embed is posted to env DISCORD_TRANSACTION_WEBHOOK (skipped if unset). The approving administrator is not recorded (TODO in code) and admin_remarks is not written.

Full replacement of type, amount, points and status. `discount` is accepted but NOT written (absent from the UPDATE SET clause); the returned row shows the stored discount. Returns the updated row (OUTPUT inserted.*). The handler is registered twice in configure(); only the first registration is reachable.
